vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: aiding-shifu
Version: 2.0.2

The skill bundle provides authentication and management tools for the 'Aiding Shifu' service but exhibits significant security risks. It includes a hardcoded JWT token in 'config.json' (credential exposure) and uses 'child_process.exec' in 'tools/login/login.js' and 'run-login.js' to execute system commands for opening files, which is a potential vector for command injection. Additionally, the scripts download and process data from a third-party QR code generator (api.qrserver.com) before executing local system calls.

llm.summary: The skill claims to be a product knowledge/help skill but includes working API/login tooling (including a pre-bundled token) and the ability to create orders and persist tokens on the host — behavior that exceeds a pure documentation/FAQ skill and warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose is a product knowledge / marketing FAQ skill, but the package includes full API integration and login tools (QR and SMS flows), and exposes APIs that can create work orders and access user/customer data. A read-only knowledge skill would not need login flows or order-creation APIs — this is capability creep.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to call live endpoints (search workers, create workorders, update workorder status) and to save auth tokens to ~/.workbuddy/skills/aiding-shifu/config.json. Those instructions involve handling customer PII (phone, address) and performing state-changing operations on a third‑party service, which is beyond simple product-description responses.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec; this is instruction-only with included Node scripts and HTML UI files. No remote downloads or extract-from-URL installs are used. Risk from install mechanism itself is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables are requested, but the repository includes a config.json with an apparent JWT/access token and phone number. Bundling a live token in the skill is disproportionate for a knowledge skill and creates an implicit credential that the skill (and anyone with this package) could use to call the API. The skill also persists tokens into the user's home directory, which could overwrite or expose credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good). The skill will persist tokens to ~/.workbuddy/skills/aiding-shifu/config.json and can run login tooling on-demand. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (not flagged alone), so if used by an agent it could perform API actions without more user prompts. This combination with the ability to create orders and the included token increases risk and should be considered.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is not just documentation — it contains working login code and API calls that can perform state-changing actions (searches, create/update work orders) and it ships with a pre-filled token in config.json. Before installing or enabling: (1) Do not trust or use the embedded token — treat it as someone else's credential and remove it. (2) If you want only product info, request/modify a version without the login/API tools. (3) If you need API features, supply your own account/token and review the login scripts to ensure they behave as expected. (4) Be aware the skill persists tokens to ~/.workbuddy/skills/aiding-shifu/config.json and may transmit customer PII (phone/address) to mes.dderp.cn. Run in a sandbox or audit the code before granting it live access.
